summary: During wizard genocide at step 594, C leaves a Bell of Opening on the floor while JavaScript removes it with the genocided monster's inventory. read.c:do_class_genocide() calls mon.c:mongone(), which calls steal.c:mdrop_special_objs() before discard_minvent(). The JS helper keeps the resistance and quest-artifact checks but records note_unported() instead of transferring a protected object. The source helper must perform the floor drop before inventory disposal; its async lifecycle must be awaited by the implemented callers.

source.branch: mdrop_special_objs() protected-object branch for a monster on the map, reached from wizard class genocide
dependencies: mon.c:mongone() calls mdrop_special_objs() before discard_minvent(); both operations must remain ordered.
steal.c:mdrop_obj() already implements extraction, floor effects, placement, stacking, and extrinsic updates; this task must wire that helper rather than duplicate it.

relevantSource.read: read.c:do_class_genocide() wizard '*' branch calls mongone() for each live monster.
relevantSource.steal: steal.c:mdrop_special_objs() retains objects for which obj_resists(obj,0,0) or is_quest_artifact(obj) is true; on-map monsters use mdrop_obj(mon,obj,FALSE).
relevantSource.zap: zap.c:obj_resists() protects invocation items such as the Bell of Opening even when both resistance chances are zero.

js.genocide: js/read.js:do_class_genocide() awaits the return from mongone() when it is a Promise.
js.gap: js/steal.js:mdrop_special_objs() records note_unported() for protected-object floor drops.
js.dropHelper: js/steal.js:mdrop_obj() already implements the source transfer lifecycle and is asynchronous.

evidence: The accepted v66 baseline identifies recording SHA d11c9aeaf45a9a82cf9e014e2ad6a461f64d34bd9532d883f2d3e71351d65a8f and reports 614/639 screens, 2931/2935 RNG calls, and 638/639 cursors matched.

Fresh bounded replay from worker HEAD 8475c19ab61b35c07bf7eb2a2ada25f3b70d9773 emits all 639 screens and reproduces the first screen mismatch at step 594, newline input: C shows the Bell glyph '(' at row 11 column 20, while JS shows floor '.'.

The replay trace reaches wizard class genocide at step 594. In C, read.c:do_class_genocide() calls mongone(); mon.c:mongone() calls mdrop_special_objs() before discard_minvent(). In JS, read.js calls mongone() and can await a returned Promise, but mon.js currently invokes the helper synchronously and then discards inventory.

The source helper preserves each inventory object when obj_resists(obj,0,0) or is_quest_artifact(obj) succeeds. Its map-resident branch calls mdrop_obj(mon,obj,FALSE), which already exists as an asynchronous JS helper; the present JS placeholder records the protected-object gap and leaves discard_minvent() to remove the Bell.
The later RNG divergence at step 617 is outside the first screen mismatch and is not attributed to this diagnosis.
